class.name: NetwSceneCore
class.brief_description: The scene column's record plane: a routing table keyed by scene identity, and the one scene request in flight.
class.description: It holds no [Node] and instantiates nothing, which is what makes a registration outlive the scene it names. A scene is identified by the entity [RID] it is keyed under rather than by whichever node is currently standing in for it, so rebuilding a scene does not silently drop everyone watching it. Everything that reaches a [Node], a [PackedScene] or a promise lives in the interface above this class. [codeblock] observe(scene, event, callback) one row per (event, scene), in registration order dispatch(scene, event, ...) every live callback; the dead ones are dropped here open_request() the next id, and it becomes the pending one is_current(id) whether a reply names the request still in flight close_request() nothing is pending again [/codeblock] A request id can only be drawn, never claimed. There is no setter for [member pending_request_id], because an id a caller could assign without opening would let it answer a request nobody made.

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every registration and the request record, and restarts the id counter. Session teardown.

method.name: close_request
method.description: Clears [member pending_request_id], so a second reply for the same request finds nothing rather than answering one that already answered.

method.name: dispatch
method.description: Calls every live callback registered for [param scene] under [param event], in registration order, passing [param present] and [param subject]. Returns how many were called. A callback whose object is gone is dropped here rather than at a sweep somebody has to remember to run, because a dispatch is the only moment the row is already being walked.

method.name: forget_scene
method.description: Drops every registration on [param scene], across every event. A scene that is gone routes nothing.

method.name: is_current
method.description: Returns whether [param request_id] is the request currently in flight. A [param request_id] of zero is never current, so a settled request cannot be settled a second time.

method.name: observe
method.description: Registers [param callback] for [param event] on [param scene]. An invalid [param scene] or an unset [param callback] registers nothing, so a later [method dispatch] can never find a row nobody meant to create. Registering the same [param callback] twice stores it once, so an edge is heard once.

method.name: observer_count
method.description: How many callbacks one row holds, counting any whose object has died since the last [method dispatch] reached them.

method.name: open_request
method.description: Draws the next request id, makes it the pending one, and returns it. Ids come from one counter, so a reply can name the request it answers and a stale reply can be told apart from the current one.

method.name: unobserve
method.description: Reverses [method observe] for one [param callback]. Removing something never registered is inert rather than an error.

members.member: The id [method open_request] will draw next.
The request currently in flight, or zero when none is. Read-only by construction: see [method open_request].
